decisionBox.changed: Position stays REDUCE and the reduction is executed rather than merely signalled, because the midday report's gate fired and kept firing. Midday required a settled 1H close below 76,192.6; the 19:00Z bar closed 76,183.9, clearing by 8.7 points, and the four bars after it closed 75,934.8, 75,448.9, 75,667.9 and 75,641.0 - five consecutive settled hourly closes beneath the level, the last of them 551.6 points through. The 75,603.0 invalidation was breached on price by 647.5 points at the 74,955.5 low and then on settled closes at 75,448.9 and 75,641.0. The 77,118.5 add gate did not fire; price traded to 77,207.0 at 18:00Z, 88.5 points above it, but the hour closed 75,999.9 and no settled close has printed above 76,183.9 since. What is genuinely NEW, and it cuts the other way, is the first two-sided liquidation print in three sessions: the 100-fill OKX window from 22:10:15Z to 00:02:04Z carries 606,423 USD of LONG liquidations clustered at 75,100 to 75,300 and 824,638 USD of SHORT liquidations at 75,600 to 75,900, and aggregate BTC open interest has fallen 3.39 percent from 2.896 billion at 17:00Z to 2.798 billion at 00:00Z while the long-short account ratio finally ticked down from its 1.83 peak to 1.79. That is the first time this month both of the conditions in the 13 September flush rule have moved the right way at once. They have moved a little, not a lot - 1.79 is still the second most crowded long reading of the month - so this is a reason to stop selling aggressively, not a reason to buy. Hence a 15 percent trim rather than the 20 percent midday took, a resting stop under the day low, and no leverage into a Fed decision.

overnightRisk: The next report is roughly 02:00 COT tomorrow and the gap between now and then contains the single largest scheduled catalyst of the month. The FOMC decides on Wednesday 16 September with the US 10-year having printed 5.041 percent intraday today, a nineteen-year high, before settling at 4.992 percent - so the bond market is pricing a Fed that cannot cut and bitcoin has spent two sessions repricing against exactly that. Three specific things can move price violently while this desk is asleep. First, the Fed statement and any dot-plot shift: a hawkish hold with the 10-year already at 5 percent is the path that breaks 74,955.5, and the measured long-liquidation pocket at 75,100 to 75,300 sits directly in the way - 606,423 USD of longs were already carried out there in the last two hours, which means stop density is proven at that shelf, not hypothetical. Second, the Saudi pipeline. Brent is 107.80 after a 21.87 percent one-month run and CNBC reports Saudi Arabia racing to restart the line; a restart headline is disinflationary and risk-positive, a second disruption headline is neither, and the move will land in thin Asian hours. Third, the ETF tape. The 15 September Farside row is a partial print at minus 288.7 million with IBIT not yet reported - FBTC alone shed 214.8 million - which breaks the one-day positive streak and means the unlevered bid that has been the floor argument since 11 September was not there today. Below 74,955.5 the next verified structure is the 4H EMA200 at 74,529.1, another 426.4 points down, and there is nothing measured between them. That gap is why the resting stop at 74,900.0 is recommended this session and was not last session: it is 916.6 points under the mark, 55.5 points under the day low, and it is the only protection that works while nobody is watching.

liquidityMagnet.note: nearestAbove is null and it is a measurement limit rather than a claim that nothing rests overhead. The filled-liquidation feed is capped at 100 fills and this window reaches back only to 22:10Z, by which time price was already under 76,000; the long liquidations that certainly printed on the 77,207.0 to 74,955.5 collapse between 18:00Z and 20:00Z have been pushed out of the window and cannot be counted, so quoting a number above price would be invention. The forward heatmap that would fill the gap needs a keyed CoinGlass source; the browser fallback was not used this run because the free OKX feed returned fresh, two-sided data rather than being blocked. What CAN be verified is the direction, and it reads down on the balance of evidence rather than unanimously. Down: the only unconsumed pocket is the 500,412 USD of long stops at 75,100 to 75,300, the account ratio is 1.79 against 1.24 at 00:00Z yesterday, and funding remains positive at 0.00589 percent per 8h so longs are still paying to hold. Against: open interest has fallen 3.39 percent from 2.896 billion at 17:00Z to 2.798 billion at 00:00Z, the ratio has come off its 1.83 peak for the first time in a day, and the perp premium is NEGATIVE at minus 0.000451, meaning the swap is trading under spot - all three are the signature of longs actually leaving rather than being replaced. Net: pull down, conviction moderate, and the balance is closer than at any point since 13 September.

etfFlows.note: Farside Investors US spot Bitcoin ETF tape, read at 19:35 COT. The 15 September row has now printed and it is NEGATIVE at minus 288.7 million, which breaks the one-session positive streak set on 14 September at plus 159.9 million. The row is PARTIAL - IBIT shows a dash rather than a figure, so the largest fund in the complex has not reported - and the minus 288.7 million is therefore built from FBTC minus 214.8, GBTC minus 44.1, ARKB minus 17.4 and BITB minus 12.4, with everything else flat. Two honest caveats follow. The number can still move materially when IBIT posts, in either direction, since IBIT has swung between plus 454.0 and minus 201.2 in the last fortnight. And the FBTC print alone at minus 214.8 million is the single largest one-day Fidelity outflow since 1 August. What it costs the bull case is specific: the floor argument used by the midnight, morning and midday sessions was that unlevered ETF money cannot be liquidated and was arriving; today it left. Eight of the last nine sessions from 08 September are now negative, totalling roughly minus 751 million against a single plus 159.9 million day.

Falling open interest, a ratio off its peak, compressing funding and a negative premium together are the signature of leveraged longs actually leaving. That is the 13 September flush rule's second condition finally moving the right way - moving, not met.

indices.bias: Very cheap on the month's own scale, and this is a NEW settled close rather than the carried Monday figure the last three reports used. QQQ closed 704.54 on Tuesday 15 September, down 4.64 points and 0.65 percent from 709.18, on 25,959,240 shares, and that close is the LOWEST of its trailing twenty-one sessions - the zero percentile, 3.47 percent under the 729.87 monthly high and 1.23 percent under the 713.31 twenty-day average, with RSI at 43.58. Three consecutive lower closes and a monthly low is the Nasdaq proxy pricing a 10-year that touched 5.041 percent; long-duration growth carries a rate shock first and this is what that looks like. For a monthly contribution the read is unchanged from midnight, morning and midday and now has better evidence behind it: this is the cheapest print of the month for a scheduled buy, it is not a call that the low is in, and there is no reason to front-run tomorrow's Fed decision to place it.

calibration.note: The midday session set a 76,192.6 reduce gate and a 77,118.5 add gate at 17:45Z. The REDUCE GATE FIRED and then kept firing. It required a settled 1H close below 76,192.6; the 19:00Z bar closed 76,183.9, clearing by 8.7 points, and the four bars after it closed 75,934.8, 75,448.9, 75,667.9 and 75,641.0 - five consecutive settled hourly closes beneath the level, the deepest 743.7 points through. The 75,603.0 INVALIDATION was breached twice over: on price at 18:45Z when the 74,955.5 low cleared it by 647.5 points, and on settled closes at 75,448.9 and 75,641.0, which is the first time this month an invalidation has broken on closes rather than only on a wick. The 77,118.5 add gate did NOT fire, and the distinction matters because price DID trade through it - the 18:00Z bar reached 77,207.0, 88.5 points above the level - before closing 75,999.9, so an add placed on price rather than on a settled close would have been filled and would now be 1,390.4 points offside. That is the third time in five sessions the settled-close requirement has paid for itself. The resting stop decision has now also resolved: midday carried 76,150.0 in the stopOrder field with recommended set to FALSE, and price cleared it by 1,194.5 points at the low. That is two consecutive sessions where an unrecommended stop would have been the right trade, which is why this session sets recommended to true. Midday published range with a BEARISH tilt at 38 bear against 22 bull and price is 968.7 points and 1.26 percent lower, so the tilt was right in direction and this time also right in size. Discretionary: midday SOLD 20 percent of the spot core at 76,785.3 and left futures flat. Spot marks 76,785.3 down to 75,816.6, so that trim avoided about 0.03 USDT of mark-to-market loss on a 28.70 USDT sleeve and moved 28.70 USDT into cash that is now worth 1.26 percent more in bitcoin terms. Hence actingHelped is TRUE - the first true since 14 September endday, and it is true for the same reason that one was: the session followed a gate it had written in advance instead of re-deciding. What has NOT resolved, and is handed forward, is the 13 September flush rule. It requires open interest AND the long-short account ratio to both fall through a one-sided flush before treating it as a floor. Tonight is the first time both have moved the right way at once - open interest minus 3.39 percent from 17:00Z to 00:00Z, ratio 1.83 down to 1.79 - but 1.79 is still the second most crowded reading of the month and the fall is 0.04. The rule has been tested five times and has not failed; this is the sixth test and it is genuinely ambiguous. The midnight session inherits it.
